title: Eight shifts in global open source

pages.subtitle: Activity, assets and a changing geography
pages.lead: AI is reshaping development workflows, open supply now spans code, models and data, and participation and contributions are growing across the Global South.

items.scope: GitHub · 12 months ending 30 September each year
items.title: AI enters the development workflow
items.body: GitHub activity expanded sharply in 2026 alongside the use of AI agents. The share of pull requests detectably authored by agents rose from 17% in March to over 40% in September. These concurrent trends point to changing workflows; they do not establish AI’s causal contribution. Quality and public value still depend on review, maintenance and adoption.

items.scope: Public repositories, models and datasets · distinct windows
items.title: Supply spans code, models and data
items.body: Adding Hugging Face broadens this edition’s view of open assets. Code repositories, models and datasets all expanded in their respective observation windows, but their counts cannot be added together. The next question is how these resources connect—and whether open outputs can be adopted, adapted and maintained over time.

items.title: A broader base for local development
items.body: Active developer counts rose by 42.0% in China, 28.4% in India and 29.2% across the six-country group. Growing participation does not imply uniform capabilities or positions in collaboration networks. Its developmental value depends on locally relevant projects, including language, education and industry needs, supported by sustained maintenance and cross-border cooperation.

items.chart_title: China overtakes the US in this series
items.title: Participation becomes contribution
items.body: In the report’s regional comparison series, China’s contribution rose from 3.008 million in 2025 to 4.429 million OpenRank in 2026, exceeding the US figure of 4.240 million. Growth thus extends from participation to measured collaboration. This crossover applies to this series’ coverage and method; project diversity, sustained supply and maintenance remain essential to interpreting it.

pages.subtitle: Cities, organizations and the agent ecosystem
pages.lead: Model reuse brings Hangzhou into focus, monthly rankings reveal shifts among enterprises and foundations, and agent tools extend across a broader range of tasks.

items.chart_title: Hangzhou stands out in model reuse
items.title: A city’s reach extends through reuse
items.body: Hangzhou ranked third in China by developer count in 2025, with about 1.62 million developers. In the five-city institutional sample, it leads in model downloads, likes and direct derivatives, driven mainly by Qwen and DeepSeek. Talent concentration and external model reuse reveal different dimensions of city influence; these rankings should be interpreted separately.

items.scope: Global enterprise monthly OpenRank · selected months
items.title: Monthly shifts reveal new momentum
items.body: Huawei overtook Microsoft in March 2026 and remained first through June. Monthly rankings locate the timing of a shift; aggregation over the main reporting period captures a different horizon. Microsoft still ranks first and Huawei second for that full period. Sustained investment and the mix of projects help interpret the monthly crossover.

items.scope: Foundation monthly OpenRank · LF family aggregated
items.title: Foundation positions are changing
items.body: The OpenAtom Foundation overtook Apache in June 2025. With the Linux Foundation and its sub-foundations aggregated, OpenAtom ranks second. This historical event is newly covered in this edition. It signals a shift in organizational collaboration; governance quality still requires evidence about project responsibilities, continuity of maintenance and actual use.

items.title: Evaluate agents across whole tasks
items.body: The landscape in §4.1 spans 86 projects in 12 categories; 48 repositories were created since January 2025. Alongside coding assistants, memory, tool connectivity, isolated execution and evaluation form a broader division of work. Assessment must extend to whole tasks: whether context persists, tools work together and results can be reliably verified.
